summary: A satirical mock policy document from Endless Frontier, Inc. describing its remote employee professional development program as a pointless, absurd exercise. It lampoons bootcamps, learning by osmosis, mentorship, gamified leaderboards, and feedback forms, concluding that employees will learn nothing useful beyond buzzword bingo and surviving PowerPoint.
one_line: A satirical parody of Endless Frontier, Inc.'s remote professional development program, mocking corporate training, mentorship, gamification, and feedback systems.
key_facts: Endless Frontier, Inc. presents its Professional Development and Training guidelines for remote employees in a satirical tone, also calling itself Endless Bureaucracy Industries.
The Virtual Bootcamp, called the Professional De-development Bootcamp, is a monthly 48-hour Zoom-a-thon described as 'mandatorily optional' and full of dense PowerPoint presentations.
Learning by Osmosis tells employees to place their training manual under their pillow and let knowledge diffuse while they snooze during working hours.
Webinars are described as having narration so monotone it sounds like 'the ghost of Ben Stein on Ambien.'
In the Mentorship Program, mentors are chosen at random from employees who lost a bet.
Mentors are reachable only by carrier pigeon between 12:01 am and 3:00 am on the fifth Sunday of every month, a day that typically does not exist.
The 'race to the bottom' leaderboard awards points for the most creative excuses for not completing training modules.
Top leaderboard scorers receive a mug reading 'World's OK-est Employee.'
The feedback system consists of forms, surveys, and automated responses; submitting a form triggers an automated 'We value your input!' message that leads to the 'virtual round file.'
The conclusion calls the program the Professional Detraining Program, saying employees will have learned nothing useful but will be adept at buzzword bingo and PowerPoint purgatory.
The document ends by joking that the only thing less productive than poorly designed remote training is reading the policy in its entirety.
